reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling campus publishes 116 MW of IT capacity across three facilities. At typical densities for mixed workloads, this could host roughly 2,320 AI accelerators if fully deployed for training, though the operator has not disclosed the actual workload split.

The campus ranks second in published capacity among Virginia's data centers. Of 330 mapped facilities statewide, only 25 publish capacity figures. Sterling represents 7.2% of Virginia's declared IT load at 1,603 MW total. This opacity matters because most of the state's infrastructure remains unquantified, making it impossible to assess whether Virginia's grid can support concentrated AI expansion.

The published specifications indicate 98 watts per square foot of technical space, consistent with a mixed deployment rather than AI-exclusive infrastructure. Whether this campus becomes significant to AI scaling depends on factors the data does not cover: grid interconnection headroom, actual workload composition, and operator expansion plans. Neither the facility's power source nor its growth trajectory appears in the public record.
